newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Nikkei futures end weak as bears reign.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Nikkei futures end weak as bears reign.

text.p: SIMEX Nikkei futures plumbed depths not seen for more than a year by the close of Wednesday's trade as bearish sentiment continued to dominate on the Tokyo market, dealers said.
The benchmark Nikkei 225 March contract ended 280 points lower at 18,680 after hitting a bottom of 18,585. The 225-share Nikkei average lost 215.81 points to close at 18,680.38.
Dealers in Tokyo said the sell-off was prompted by worries over the bad loan problems of companies in the construction, securities and banking sectors.
A Singapore-based trader said the March Nikkei's decline was exacerbated by stop-loss sales around the 18,750 level.
"It's still on the weak side. The next level to watch is 18,500," he said, adding that a break below that level could push the contract down to 18,150.
"The market is really wary now. It's moved down 700-800 points in the last few days. There's bound to be some bargain hunters emerging," he added.
